name: Hyde Park & Kensington Gardens
description: The classic central London loop: the Serpentine, Kensington Palace and the Italian Gardens.

messages.text: The Serpentine lake was created in 1730 for Queen Caroline.
Kensington Palace is just here, where Queen Victoria was born.
Speakers' Corner. People have gathered to speak their minds here since the 1870s.

name: Regent's Park & Primrose Hill
description: Round the Outer Circle and up Primrose Hill for one of London's best skyline views.

messages.text: Top of Primrose Hill. Take a second for the view across London. You earned it.

name: Thames Bridges Loop
description: South Bank out to Tower Bridge, back along the north bank to Westminster.

messages.text: Tate Modern, once Bankside Power Station, opened as a gallery in 2000.
Crossing Tower Bridge, opened in 1894. Mind the tourists.

name: Richmond Park Gates Loop
description: A big loop linking the park's gates. Rolling hills, open grassland and deer.

messages.text: Richmond Park is home to hundreds of red and fallow deer. Give them plenty of space.

name: Hampstead Heath Hills
description: Parliament Hill, the heath and the ponds. Hilly, green and a proper workout.

messages.text: Parliament Hill. Look for St Paul's Cathedral on the skyline.

name: Victoria Park Loop
description: Flat, fast laps of the East End's People's Park.

messages.text: Victoria Park opened in 1845 and is known as the People's Park.

name: Greenwich Park & Cutty Sark
description: From the Cutty Sark up to the Royal Observatory and round the park.

messages.text: The Cutty Sark, a tea clipper built in 1869.
The Royal Observatory, home of the Prime Meridian, longitude zero.

name: Battersea Park
description: A flat riverside loop past the Peace Pagoda.

messages.text: The Peace Pagoda by the river was built in 1985.

name: Clapham Common
description: A short, flat loop of the common. Good for an easy run or intervals.

name: Wimbledon Common Trails
description: Woodland and heath trails from the Windmill.

messages.text: Wimbledon Windmill dates from 1817.

name: Queen Elizabeth Olympic Park
description: Past the stadium, the Orbit and the Velodrome of the London 2012 Games.

messages.text: The London Stadium, centrepiece of the 2012 Olympic Games.

name: Bushy Park
description: Wide open paths, the Diana Fountain and Chestnut Avenue.

messages.text: The Diana Fountain, on Chestnut Avenue, laid out by Christopher Wren.

name: Crystal Palace Park
description: A hilly little loop with Victorian dinosaurs.

messages.text: The Crystal Palace dinosaur sculptures were unveiled in 1854.

name: Regent's Canal Towpath
description: Little Venice to King's Cross along the canal, via Camden Lock.

messages.text: Camden Lock. Watch for walkers and bikes on the narrow towpath.
Nearly there. The Regent's Canal opened in 1820.

name: Kew to Richmond Thames Path
description: A riverside run from Kew Bridge, past Kew Gardens, to Richmond Bridge.

messages.text: Richmond Bridge, the oldest surviving bridge across the Thames in London.

name: Alexandra Palace Park
description: Hill repeats with a view: a loop of the park below Ally Pally.

messages.text: Alexandra Palace hosted the first regular BBC television broadcasts in 1936.

name: Mote Park Loop
description: Round the lake and across the rolling parkland of Maidstone's biggest park.

name: Canterbury Walls & Great Stour
description: Westgate Gardens and the Great Stour Way, then back along the city walls and through the old centre.

messages.text: The Westgate, built around 1380, is the largest surviving city gate in England.

name: Whitstable to Herne Bay
description: Along the coast from Whitstable harbour past Tankerton Slopes and Swalecliffe to Herne Bay pier.

messages.text: Look out to sea for The Street, a shingle bank that appears at low tide.

name: Margate to Broadstairs Clifftops
description: The Viking Coastal Trail from Turner Contemporary past Botany Bay and Kingsgate to Viking Bay.

messages.text: Turner Contemporary, the gallery named after the painter J. M. W. Turner, opened in 2011.
Viking Bay, Broadstairs. Charles Dickens spent many summers here.

name: Broadstairs to Ramsgate
description: The clifftop path from Viking Bay past Dumpton Gap to the Royal Harbour at Ramsgate.

messages.text: Ramsgate is a Royal Harbour, a title granted by King George the Fourth in 1821.

name: Folkestone Leas & Coastal Park
description: West along the clifftop Leas, back through the Lower Leas Coastal Park and up through the old town.

name: Hythe Canal & Seafront
description: East along the Royal Military Canal towards Seabrook, back beside the sea on Princes Parade.

messages.text: The Royal Military Canal was dug from 1804 as a defence against invasion by Napoleon.

name: White Cliffs of Dover
description: Clifftop chalk grassland from the National Trust centre past South Foreland Lighthouse to St Margaret's.

messages.text: On a clear day you can see France, about 21 miles across the Channel.

name: Deal to Kingsdown Seafront
description: A flat seafront run past Deal Pier and the Deal and Walmer castles to the shingle at Kingsdown.

messages.text: Deal Castle, one of the coastal forts Henry the Eighth built around 1540.

name: Tunbridge Wells Common & Pantiles
description: From the Pantiles across the Common past Wellington Rocks and back through Calverley Grounds.

messages.text: The Pantiles grew up around the chalybeate spring discovered here in 1606.

name: Knole Park
description: Rolling tracks round the ancient deer park that surrounds Knole house.

messages.text: Knole is home to wild fallow and sika deer. Give them plenty of space.

name: Bedgebury Forest Trails
description: Wide forest tracks through the pine plantations of Bedgebury Forest, beside the National Pinetum.

name: Rochester to Chatham Riverside
description: Past Rochester Castle and the cathedral, then along the Medway riverside walk towards the Historic Dockyard at Chatham.

messages.text: Rochester Cathedral was founded in 604, making it the second oldest in England.

name: Capstone Farm Country Park
description: Quiet paths over the grassy chalk slopes and woodland of Capstone Farm Country Park.

name: Gravesend Riverside
description: Along the Thames promenade to the canal basin and back through the old town.

messages.text: St George's Church is close by. Pocahontas was buried there in 1617.

name: Herne Bay to Reculver
description: East from Herne Bay pier along the Oyster Bay Trail to the twin towers at Reculver.

messages.text: The twin towers of Reculver's ruined church have been a landmark for sailors for centuries.

name: Ashford Victoria Park & Stour
description: A short town run from Victoria Park along the Great Stour and Ashford's green corridor.

name: Lullingstone Country Park
description: Riverside meadows and chalk hillside in the Darent Valley.

messages.text: Lullingstone Roman Villa lies just along this valley.

name: Tonbridge Castle to Haysden
description: West along the River Medway from Tonbridge Castle to Haysden Country Park, back through town.

name: Shorne Woods Country Park
description: Woodland trails and heathland in a country park between Gravesend and Rochester.

name: Brighton & Hove Seafront
description: Flat and fast along the promenade from Black Rock, past both piers, to Hove Lagoon.

messages.text: Brighton Palace Pier, opened in 1899.
The skeleton of the West Pier, which opened in 1866.

name: Undercliff Walk to Saltdean
description: From Brighton Marina along the sea wall below the chalk cliffs to Rottingdean and Saltdean.

messages.text: Stay on the walkway. Chalk can fall from the cliffs above.

name: Stanmer Park & Great Wood
description: Up from Stanmer House into Stanmer Great Wood and back down across the parkland.

name: Ditchling Beacon to Devil's Dyke
description: A ridge run along the South Downs Way, past the Jack and Jill windmills, to Devil's Dyke.

messages.text: Ditchling Beacon, the highest point in East Sussex.
The Jack and Jill windmills are a short way off the path here.

name: Cuckmere Haven & Seven Sisters
description: Down the Cuckmere valley to the beach, up onto the first of the Seven Sisters and back inland.

messages.text: Clifftop section. Keep well back from the edge, it can crumble without warning.

name: Beachy Head & Birling Gap
description: A clifftop loop past Belle Tout lighthouse to Birling Gap, returning over open downland.

messages.text: Keep well back from the cliff edge on this stretch.
Belle Tout lighthouse, moved back from the crumbling cliff edge in 1999.

name: Eastbourne Seafront
description: The long flat promenade from Holywell, past the pier, to Sovereign Harbour.

messages.text: The Wish Tower, a Martello tower built to guard against Napoleonic invasion.

name: Hastings to Bexhill Promenade
description: From Hastings Pier through St Leonards and along the coast to Bexhill's De La Warr Pavilion.

messages.text: The De La Warr Pavilion, a modernist landmark opened in 1935.

name: Rye Harbour & Camber Castle
description: Out along the River Rother to Rye Harbour and back across the nature reserve past Camber Castle.

messages.text: Camber Castle, one of the coastal forts built by Henry the Eighth.

name: Lewes Railway Land & Castle
description: A short loop of the county town past the Railway Land nature reserve, Southover and the castle.

messages.text: Lewes Castle was built soon after the Norman Conquest.

name: Ashdown Forest from Gills Lap
description: Open heathland tracks and pine clumps on the high ground of Ashdown Forest.

messages.text: Ashdown Forest inspired the Hundred Acre Wood in A. A. Milne's Winnie-the-Pooh stories.

name: Forest Way Railway Path
description: A gentle, traffic-free run along an old railway line from East Grinstead past Forest Row.

messages.text: The Forest Way follows the line of a railway that closed in the 1960s.

name: Worthing Seafront
description: Flat promenade running from Goring, past Worthing Pier, towards East Worthing.

messages.text: Worthing Pier, first opened in 1862.

name: Littlehampton Seafront & River Arun
description: Along the promenade to the harbour mouth, up the River Arun and over the footbridge to the West Beach path.

name: Arundel Park & Swanbourne Lake
description: Out past Swanbourne Lake, then a hilly loop over the open grassland of Arundel Park.

messages.text: Arundel Castle, seat of the Dukes of Norfolk.

name: Chichester Walls & Canal
description: Round the old city walls, then out along the Chichester Canal towpath towards Hunston.

messages.text: Chichester's city walls follow the line of the Roman town defences.

name: Bognor Regis Seafront
description: A flat run along the promenade from West Bognor, past the pier, to Felpham.

messages.text: The town became Bognor Regis after King George the Fifth convalesced here in 1929.

name: Tilgate Park
description: Lakeside paths and woodland tracks on the southern edge of Crawley.

name: Horsham Park & Chesworth Farm
description: From Horsham Park through the old town and out along the River Arun to Chesworth Farm.

name: Petworth Park
description: Rolling grassland and lakes in the deer park landscaped by Capability Brown.

messages.text: Petworth Park is home to a large herd of fallow deer. Give them plenty of space.

name: Cissbury Ring
description: A hilly downland loop up to and around the ramparts of Cissbury Ring.

messages.text: Cissbury Ring, an Iron Age hillfort built over much older Neolithic flint mines.

name: Box Hill & the Stepping Stones
description: Across the River Mole on the stepping stones, then a steep climb to the viewpoint over Dorking.

messages.text: The Box Hill viewpoint. Jane Austen set the picnic scene in Emma up here.

name: Leith Hill Tower Loop
description: Woodland tracks and a quiet lane up to the Gothic tower on top of Leith Hill.

messages.text: Leith Hill Tower, built in 1765.

name: Headley Heath
description: Sandy heathland tracks and short, sharp hills on the edge of the North Downs.

name: Ranmore Common
description: Woodland paths and tracks on Ranmore Common, high on the North Downs above Dorking.

name: Epsom Downs
description: Open chalk downland around the racecourse, from Tattenham Corner past the grandstand.

messages.text: Tattenham Corner. The Derby has been run on these downs since 1780.

name: Priory Park & Reigate Heath
description: From Priory Park out along quiet lanes to the open heath and back through the old town.

name: St Martha's Hill & Newlands Corner
description: Sandy North Downs Way tracks from the Newlands Corner viewpoint to St Martha's hilltop church.

name: Guildford to Godalming by the Wey
description: Riverside towpath from Millmead Lock in Guildford, past Shalford meadows, to Godalming Wharf.

name: Frensham Little Pond
description: Sandy heath trails and a quiet lane around Frensham Little Pond and Frensham Common.

name: Devil's Punch Bowl
description: Round the rim of the Punch Bowl and up to Gibbet Hill, with a descent into the valley.

messages.text: The old A3 ran across this hillside until the Hindhead Tunnel opened in 2011.

name: Virginia Water Lake
description: A flat loop of the lake in Windsor Great Park, past the Cascade waterfall.

name: Staines to Runnymede Thames Path
description: Upstream from Staines Bridge past Bell Weir Lock to the water meadows at Runnymede.

messages.text: Runnymede. King John agreed to Magna Carta in these meadows in 1215.

name: Horsell Common
description: Pine woods and heath trails on the common where H. G. Wells landed his Martians.

messages.text: In The War of the Worlds, the first Martian cylinder lands on Horsell Common.

name: Chobham Common
description: Wide sandy tracks across open lowland heath and birch scrub.

name: Farnham Park
description: Rolling parkland below Farnham Castle, with views back over the town.

messages.text: Farnham Castle, just below, was built by the Bishops of Winchester in the twelfth century.

name: Wey Navigation: Weybridge to Pyrford
description: A quiet towpath run from Thames Lock at Weybridge past Coxes Lock and New Haw to Pyrford Lock.

messages.text: Thames Lock. The River Wey Navigation, opened in 1653, starts here.

name: Basingstoke Canal Towpath
description: From the canal centre at Mytchett along the towpath and down the Deepcut lock flight towards Brookwood.

messages.text: The Basingstoke Canal opened in 1794.

name: Norbury Park
description: Woodland and farmland tracks above the Mole valley, through the old yews of Druids Grove.

name: Esher Commons & Oxshott Heath
description: Heath and woodland trails from Black Pond across to the sandy ridge of Oxshott Heath.

name: Walton to Hampton Court Thames Path
description: A flat riverside run from Walton Bridge, round the big bend past Hurst Park, to Hampton Court Bridge.

messages.text: Hampton Court Bridge. Hampton Court Palace, a favourite home of Henry VIII, is just across the river.

name: Holmbury Hill
description: A steep climb from Holmbury St Mary to an Iron Age hill fort with long views south.

turns.onto: Holmbury Hill Road to Horsham Road

messages.text: The top of Holmbury Hill, the site of an Iron Age hill fort.

name: Southsea Seafront
description: Along the promenade from the Round Tower in Old Portsmouth, past Southsea Castle, to Eastney.

messages.text: Southsea Castle was built by Henry VIII in 1544.

name: Southampton Common
description: A loop of the common on its woodland paths and open grassland, north of the city centre.

name: Weston Shore to Royal Victoria Country Park
description: Along Southampton Water from Weston Shore, past Netley, to the old military hospital chapel.

messages.text: The chapel ahead is all that remains of the Royal Victoria Military Hospital.

name: Winchester Water Meadows & St Catherine's Hill
description: From the cathedral along the Itchen Navigation beside the water meadows, with a climb of St Catherine's Hill.

messages.text: John Keats walked these water meadows in 1819 and wrote To Autumn.

name: Queen Elizabeth Country Park
description: Hilly forest tracks through the beech woods of the South Downs, from the visitor centre.

name: Lymington to Keyhaven Sea Wall
description: The sea wall path past the salt marshes and lagoons, with the Isle of Wight across the water.

messages.text: Out at the end of the shingle spit is Hurst Castle, built by Henry VIII.

name: Brockenhurst Forest Loop
description: Gravel forest tracks and open lawns north of Brockenhurst, starting from Balmer Lawn.

messages.text: New Forest ponies roam free here. Give them space and please do not feed them.

name: Lyndhurst & Bolton's Bench
description: Open heath and woodland paths east of Bolton's Bench, on the edge of the New Forest's main village.

messages.text: Ponies, cattle and donkeys have right of way in the forest. Pass them slowly and never feed them.

name: Alice Holt Forest
description: Wide gravel forest roads through oak and conifer woodland near the Surrey border.

name: Basingstoke Canal at Odiham
description: A flat towpath run from Broad Oak past Colt Hill wharf and the ruins of Odiham Castle to Greywell Tunnel.

messages.text: Local tradition says King John set out from Odiham Castle to seal Magna Carta in 1215.

name: Basingstoke Canal at Fleet
description: A flat, wooded towpath from Pondtail through Fleet towards Crookham.

name: Stokes Bay to Lee-on-the-Solent
description: Round the promenade at Stokes Bay and along the shore past Browndown to Lee-on-the-Solent.

name: Hayling Billy Trail
description: A flat, traffic-free run from Langstone down the old railway line beside Langstone Harbour.

messages.text: This trail follows the old Hayling Island branch line, which closed in 1963.

name: Emsworth to Langstone
description: From Emsworth millpond past Warblington church to the Royal Oak on the shore at Langstone.

name: Titchfield Canal to Lee-on-the-Solent
description: Down the old canal path beside Titchfield Haven to the sea at Hill Head, then along the Solent to Lee.

name: Cowes to Gurnard
description: Along the Parade and the sea wall past Egypt Point, looking out over the Solent.

messages.text: Cowes Castle, now home to the Royal Yacht Squadron, was built by Henry VIII.

name: Newport to Cowes Cycleway
description: A flat, traffic-free old railway path beside the River Medina from Newport towards Cowes.

name: Ryde Seafront to Seaview
description: East along the seafront past Appley Tower and Puckpool Park to Seaview.

messages.text: Ryde Pier first opened in 1814.

name: Sandown to Shanklin Esplanade
description: A flat sea wall run from Sandown pier along the bay to Shanklin esplanade.

name: Tennyson Down to the Needles
description: Up the chalk ridge from Freshwater Bay over Tennyson Down to the Needles headland.

messages.text: The cross on the summit is a memorial to Alfred, Lord Tennyson, who lived at Farringford below.

name: Windsor Long Walk & Great Park
description: Down the Long Walk from Windsor Castle to the Copper Horse, back through the deer park.

messages.text: The Copper Horse, a statue of King George the Third, stands at the end of the Long Walk.

name: Reading to Sonning
description: The Thames Path from Caversham Bridge, over the mouth of the Kennet and out to Sonning Lock.

messages.text: Crossing Horseshoe Bridge, where the River Kennet joins the Thames.

name: Dinton Pastures Lakes
description: A flat loop of paths between the old gravel-pit lakes of Dinton Pastures Country Park.

name: Swinley Forest & Caesar's Camp
description: Pine forest trails from the Look Out to the Iron Age hillfort at Caesar's Camp.

messages.text: Caesar's Camp is an Iron Age hillfort, despite the Roman name.

name: Newbury Kennet & Avon Canal
description: West from Newbury Lock along the Kennet & Avon towpath to Hamstead Lock.

name: Greenham Common
description: Open heathland on the old air base, with wide tracks and big skies.

messages.text: Greenham Common was an air base, famous for the women's peace camp of the 1980s.

name: Maidenhead to Cookham
description: The Thames Path from Boulter's Lock along Cliveden Reach to Cookham Bridge.

messages.text: Cliveden House sits on the wooded cliffs across the river.

name: Burnham Beeches
description: Ancient beech woodland on quiet drives and paths, past the ponds.

messages.text: The City of London has looked after Burnham Beeches since 1880.

name: Black Park Lake & Woods
description: Round the lake and through the pine woods next to Pinewood Studios.

messages.text: Pinewood Studios is next door, and these woods have appeared in many films.

name: Marlow to Bourne End
description: From the suspension bridge past Marlow Lock and along the Thames Path to Bourne End.

messages.text: Marlow's suspension bridge opened in 1832.

name: Coombe Hill from Wendover
description: A Chilterns climb from Wendover to the monument on Coombe Hill and back through the woods.

messages.text: The monument on Coombe Hill remembers men from Buckinghamshire who died in the Boer War.

name: Chess Valley Walk
description: Out of Chesham along the chalk-stream River Chess towards Latimer.

name: Willen Lake
description: Flat, fast paths round both halves of Willen Lake, past the Peace Pagoda.

messages.text: The Peace Pagoda was built by Buddhist monks and nuns and completed in 1980.

name: Port Meadow & Godstow
description: Across the ancient common to Godstow and back down the Thames.

messages.text: The ruins of Godstow Abbey stand by the river here.
Port Meadow is common grazing land, recorded in the Domesday Book.

name: Christ Church Meadow & the Isis
description: Down the towpath opposite the college boathouses to Donnington Bridge, back up the other bank to Christ Church Meadow.

messages.text: Christ Church was founded by King Henry the Eighth in 1546.
In Oxford this stretch of the Thames is known as the Isis.

name: Henley Regatta Course
description: From Henley Bridge along the Remenham bank of the regatta course, back by quiet lanes.

messages.text: Henley Royal Regatta has been held on this stretch since 1839.

name: Wittenham Clumps & Day's Lock
description: From Dorchester over the Thames at Day's Lock and up to the Clumps for wide views.

messages.text: Castle Hill, the eastern clump, is topped by an Iron Age hillfort.

name: Shotover Country Park
description: Hilly woodland and heath trails on the edge of Oxford.

name: The Ridgeway to Wayland's Smithy
description: Along the chalk ridge past Uffington Castle and the White Horse to Wayland's Smithy.

messages.text: Uffington Castle is an Iron Age hillfort. The White Horse below it dates from the Bronze Age.
Wayland's Smithy is a Neolithic long barrow.

name: Banbury Oxford Canal
description: The Oxford Canal towpath through Banbury, past Tooley's Boatyard.
